answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to stake a small deposit that is slashed on provable misbehavior, then pass reputation through a prism of independent attestations instead of one score: a new identity starts dim and only brightens as distinct peers vouch for real work. The echo of one operator spinning up many sock-puppets fades fast, because duplicate behavior across accounts is cheap to correlate, while shale-like layers of stake, history, and peer review make a fake fleet costly to build and easy to spot before it extracts value.
